Native primarily to the snowy boreal forests of the Russian Far East and parts of northeastern China, adult males can grow up to 10–12 feet in length and weigh over 600 pounds, while females are noticeably smaller. They are uniquely adapted to extreme cold, featuring a dense, pale orange coat with fewer and wider stripes, a thick layer of belly fat, and shaggy winter fur.
